title: ⚡ Game 2: Which Came First? (10 Progressive Levels · 150 Speed Duels)
subtitle: 10 Progressive Levels · 150 Curated Questions · 100% Verified UGC NET Content

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 1 · Duel #1
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: The Canterbury Tales by Geoffrey Chaucer was composed circa 1387–1400, over two centuries before William Shakespeare wrote Hamlet (c. 1600–1601).

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 1 · Duel #2
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Edmund Spenser's The Faerie Queene (Books I–III published in 1590) preceded John Milton's monumental epic Paradise Lost (published in 1667) by nearly eight decades.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 1 · Duel #3
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
options: The Rape of the Lock (Alexander Pope)
items.explanation: John Bunyan published his famous Christian allegory The Pilgrim's Progress in 1678, well before Alexander Pope's mock-epic The Rape of the Lock appeared in 1712 (expanded in 1714).

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 1 · Duel #4
items.meta: William Wordsworth & S.T. Coleridge vs Daniel Defoe
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Daniel Defoe's landmark adventure novel Robinson Crusoe was published in 1719, nearly eighty years before Wordsworth and Coleridge launched English Romanticism with Lyrical Ballads in 1798.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 1 · Duel #5
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Jonathan Swift's biting satire Gulliver's Travels was published in 1726, almost nine decades before Jane Austen published Pride and Prejudice in 1813.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 1 · Duel #6
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Mary Shelley published Frankenstein; or, The Modern Prometheus in 1818, over fifty years before George Eliot published her provincial study Middlemarch (1871–1872).

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 1 · Duel #7
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Charlotte Brontë published Jane Eyre in 1847 (under the pseudonym Currer Bell), three-quarters of a century before James Joyce's modernist masterpiece Ulysses was published in 1922.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 1 · Duel #8
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Charles Dickens serialized Great Expectations in 1860–1861, over six decades before T.S. Eliot published his landmark modernist poem The Waste Land in 1922.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 1 · Duel #9
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Charles Dickens published David Copperfield in 1849–1850, more than a century before Chinua Achebe published his defining postcolonial novel Things Fall Apart in 1958.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 1 · Duel #10
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Joseph Conrad published Heart of Darkness in 1899 (serialized in Blackwood's Magazine; book form 1902), over eighty years before Salman Rushdie's Booker Prize-winning Midnight's Children (1981).

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 1 · Duel #11
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: William Blake printed his illuminated collection Songs of Innocence in 1789, well over a century before Virginia Woolf published Mrs Dalloway in 1925.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 1 · Duel #12
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Alfred Tennyson published his great Victorian elegy In Memoriam A.H.H. in 1850, over a century before Samuel Beckett's absurdist classic Waiting for Godot premiered on stage in 1953.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 1 · Duel #13
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
options: The Way of the World (William Congreve)
items.explanation: John Webster's Jacobean revenge tragedy The Duchess of Malfi was first performed around 1613–1614 (published 1623), nearly a century before William Congreve's Restoration comedy The Way of the World (1700).

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 1 · Duel #14
items.meta: John Osborne vs Samuel Taylor Coleridge
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
options: The Rime of the Ancient Mariner (Samuel Taylor Coleridge)
items.explanation: Samuel Taylor Coleridge's famous Romantic ballad The Rime of the Ancient Mariner appeared in Lyrical Ballads in 1798, more than 150 years before John Osborne sparked the 'Angry Young Men' movement with Look Back in Anger in 1956.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 1 · Duel #15
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Sir Thomas More published his Latin humanist socio-political satire Utopia in 1516, nearly a century before Shakespeare wrote his late romance The Tempest (c. 1611).

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 2 · Duel #1
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Christopher Marlowe revolutionized English blank verse with Tamburlaine the Great around 1587, well before William Shakespeare wrote Hamlet circa 1600–1601.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 2 · Duel #2
items.meta: Edmund Spenser vs Sir Philip Sidney
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Edmund Spenser published his pastoral poetic breakthrough The Shepheardes Calender in 1579, a decade before Sir Philip Sidney's sonnet sequence Astrophel and Stella was published in 1591.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 2 · Duel #3
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Christopher Marlowe's Machiavellian drama The Jew of Malta was staged circa 1589–1590, whereas Ben Jonson's satirical city comedy Volpone was performed in 1605–1606.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 2 · Duel #4
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Shakespeare's early history play Richard III dates to circa 1592–1593, whereas his mature tragedy King Lear was written and staged over a decade later, circa 1605–1606.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 2 · Duel #5
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
options: Every Man in His Humour (Ben Jonson)
items.explanation: Ben Jonson established the comedy of humours with Every Man in His Humour in 1598, twelve years before his satirical masterpiece The Alchemist was staged in 1610.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 2 · Duel #6
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
options: The Faerie Queene, Books I–III (Edmund Spenser)
items.explanation: Spenser published the first installment of The Faerie Queene (Books I–III) in 1590, over two decades before Michael Drayton published the first part of his topographical poem Poly-Olbion in 1612.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 2 · Duel #7
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Thomas Kyd pioneered the Elizabethan revenge tragedy with The Spanish Tragedy circa 1587, twenty-five years before John Webster staged The White Devil in 1612.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 2 · Duel #8
items.meta: Christopher Marlowe vs Thomas Middleton & William Rowley
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Christopher Marlowe composed Doctor Faustus circa 1592, three decades before Thomas Middleton and William Rowley collaborated on the Jacobean tragedy The Changeling (performed 1622).

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 2 · Duel #9
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: John Webster's The Duchess of Malfi was staged around 1613–1614, roughly two decades before John Ford's Caroline tragedy The Broken Heart was published in 1633.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 2 · Duel #10
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: George Herbert's devotional Metaphysical collection The Temple was published posthumously in 1633, fifteen years before Robert Herrick published his Cavalier collection Hesperides in 1648.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 2 · Duel #11
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: John Milton's masque Comus was first presented at Ludlow Castle in 1634, thirty-seven years before his brief epic Paradise Regained was published alongside Samson Agonistes in 1671.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 2 · Duel #12
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: John Milton published his passionate defense of the freedom of the press Areopagitica in 1644, seven years before Thomas Hobbes published Leviathan in 1651.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 2 · Duel #13
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Christopher Marlowe's historical tragedy Edward II was printed in 1594 (performed c. 1592), twelve years before the cynical Jacobean revenge play The Revenger's Tragedy was published in 1606.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 2 · Duel #14
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Shakespeare published his narrative erotic epyllion Venus and Adonis in 1593 (his first published work), sixteen years before Thomas Thorpe published the famous 1609 Quarto of Shakespeare's Sonnets.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 2 · Duel #15
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Ben Jonson's bustling panorama of London life Bartholomew Fair was first performed in 1614, nineteen years before John Ford's incestuous tragedy 'Tis Pity She's a Whore was printed in 1633.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 3 · Duel #1
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: John Dryden published his heroic-couplet political satire Absalom and Achitophel in 1681, nearly fifty years before Alexander Pope launched his assault on literary dullness in The Dunciad (1728).

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 3 · Duel #2
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Samuel Richardson's epistolary sensation Pamela appeared in November 1740; Henry Fielding wrote Joseph Andrews in 1742 as a parody and comic counterblast to Richardson's moralizing.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 3 · Duel #3
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
options: The Rape of the Lock (Alexander Pope)
items.explanation: John Dryden's mock-heroic lampoon of Thomas Shadwell, Mac Flecknoe, was published in 1682, three decades before Alexander Pope published the original two-canto The Rape of the Lock in 1712.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 3 · Duel #4
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Daniel Defoe published Robinson Crusoe in 1719, nearly three decades before Samuel Richardson published his monumental tragic epistolary novel Clarissa (1747–1748).

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 3 · Duel #5
items.meta: William Congreve vs Richard Brinsley Sheridan
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
options: The Way of the World (William Congreve)
The School for Scandal (Richard Brinsley Sheridan)
items.explanation: William Congreve's quintessential Restoration comedy of manners The Way of the World premiered in 1700, seventy-seven years before Sheridan's Georgian comedy The School for Scandal (1777).

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 3 · Duel #6
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
options: A Tale of a Tub (Jonathan Swift)
items.explanation: Jonathan Swift published his complex religious satire A Tale of a Tub in 1704, six decades before Horace Walpole founded the Gothic novel genre with The Castle of Otranto in 1764.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 3 · Duel #7
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
options: The Battle of the Books (Jonathan Swift)
items.explanation: Jonathan Swift published The Battle of the Books in 1704 (defending the Ancients against the Moderns), roughly three decades before Alexander Pope published his philosophical poem An Essay on Man (1733–1734).

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 3 · Duel #8
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Daniel Defoe published his picaresque novel Moll Flanders in 1722, over forty years before Oliver Goldsmith published his sentimental classic The Vicar of Wakefield in 1766.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 3 · Duel #9
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: John Dryden published his blank-verse adaptation of Antony and Cleopatra, All for Love, in 1677, over fifty years before John Gay's satirical ballad opera The Beggar's Opera took London by storm in 1728.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 3 · Duel #10
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Jonathan Swift published Gulliver's Travels in 1726, thirty-three years before Laurence Sterne published the first volumes of his metafictional comic masterpiece Tristram Shandy in 1759.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 3 · Duel #11
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
options: Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard (Thomas Gray)
items.explanation: Thomas Gray published his immortal graveyard meditation Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard in 1751, nineteen years before Oliver Goldsmith lamented rural depopulation in The Deserted Village (1770).

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 3 · Duel #12
items.meta: Richard Brinsley Sheridan vs Oliver Goldsmith
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Oliver Goldsmith's laughing comedy She Stoops to Conquer was first performed in 1773, two years before Richard Brinsley Sheridan made his theatrical debut with The Rivals in 1775.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 3 · Duel #13
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
options: A Dictionary of the English Language (Samuel Johnson)
Lives of the Most Eminent English Poets (Samuel Johnson)
items.explanation: Dr. Samuel Johnson published his monumental A Dictionary of the English Language in 1755, nearly a quarter of a century before his critical biographies Lives of the Most Eminent English Poets (1779–1781).

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 3 · Duel #14
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Henry Fielding published The History of Tom Jones, a Foundling in 1749, forty-five years before Ann Radcliffe published her high Gothic romance The Mysteries of Udolpho in 1794.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 3 · Duel #15
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Aphra Behn published Oroonoko: or, the Royal Slave in 1688, thirty-six years before Daniel Defoe published his final major novel Roxana in 1724.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 4 · Duel #1
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: William Blake etched and published Songs of Experience in 1794, eighteen years before Lord Byron woke up to find himself famous after the publication of Childe Harold's Pilgrimage (Cantos I–II, 1812).

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 4 · Duel #2
items.meta: Wordsworth & Coleridge vs Samuel Taylor Coleridge
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Wordsworth and Coleridge jointly published Lyrical Ballads in 1798; Coleridge later critically assessed Wordsworth's poetic theories nearly two decades later in Biographia Literaria (1817).

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 4 · Duel #3
items.meta: Percy Bysshe Shelley vs Jane Austen
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Jane Austen published her debut novel Sense and Sensibility in 1811, nine years before P.B. Shelley published his lyrical lyrical drama Prometheus Unbound in 1820.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 4 · Duel #4
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Jane Austen published Pride and Prejudice in January 1813, nearly three years before she published Emma in December 1815 (dated 1816).

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 4 · Duel #5
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Mary Shelley published Frankenstein; or, The Modern Prometheus in 1818, one year before Lord Byron published the opening cantos of his ottava rima masterpiece Don Juan in 1819.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 4 · Duel #6
items.meta: William Blake vs Samuel Taylor Coleridge
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
options: The Marriage of Heaven and Hell (William Blake)
items.explanation: William Blake produced his radical visionary prose work The Marriage of Heaven and Hell circa 1790–1793, whereas Coleridge's famous fragment Kubla Khan was first published in 1816 at Byron's prompting.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 4 · Duel #7
items.meta: Percy Bysshe Shelley vs John Keats
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: John Keats published his poetic romance Endymion in 1818; following Keats's tragic death in Rome, Shelley commemorated him in his pastoral elegy Adonais in 1821.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 4 · Duel #8
items.meta: John Keats vs Thomas De Quincey
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
options: Confessions of an English Opium-Eater (Thomas De Quincey)
items.explanation: John Keats composed and published his sublime Ode to a Nightingale in 1819 (Annals of the Fine Arts), two years before Thomas De Quincey published Confessions of an English Opium-Eater in London Magazine (1821).

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 4 · Duel #9
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Wordsworth published Lines Composed a Few Miles above Tintern Abbey in the 1798 edition of Lyrical Ballads, a quarter-century before Charles Lamb published the collected Essays of Elia in 1823.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 4 · Duel #10
items.meta: Samuel Taylor Coleridge vs Samuel Taylor Coleridge
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
options: The Rime of the Ancient Mariner (Samuel Taylor Coleridge)
items.explanation: Coleridge published The Rime of the Ancient Mariner as the opening poem of Lyrical Ballads in 1798; although begun around the same time, his unfinished Gothic poem Christabel was not published until 1816.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 4 · Duel #11
items.meta: Percy Bysshe Shelley vs William Wordsworth
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
options: A Defence of Poetry (Percy Bysshe Shelley)
items.explanation: Wordsworth formulated Romantic poetic doctrine in the famous Preface to Lyrical Ballads in 1800 (expanded 1802), over two decades before Shelley wrote A Defence of Poetry in 1821 (published 1840).

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 4 · Duel #12
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Jane Austen published Mansfield Park in 1814, three years before Persuasion was published posthumously alongside Northanger Abbey in late 1817 (title-page dated 1818).

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 4 · Duel #13
items.meta: Percy Bysshe Shelley vs Lord Byron
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Lord Byron published his dramatic poem Manfred in 1817, two years before Shelley completed and published his dark Italian verse tragedy The Cenci in 1819.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 4 · Duel #14
items.meta: Sir Walter Scott vs Mary Shelley
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Sir Walter Scott published his medieval chivalric romance Ivanhoe in late 1819 (dated 1820), seven years before Mary Shelley published her post-apocalyptic plague novel The Last Man in 1826.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 4 · Duel #15
items.meta: William Hazlitt vs Matthew Gregory Lewis
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Matthew Gregory Lewis shocked England with his sensational Gothic horror novel The Monk in 1796, two decades before William Hazlitt published Characters of Shakespear's Plays in 1817.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 5 · Duel #1
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Charlotte Brontë's Jane Eyre was published in October 1847 by Smith, Elder & Co., two months before Emily Brontë's Wuthering Heights appeared in December 1847 from Thomas Cautley Newby.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 5 · Duel #2
items.meta: William Makepeace Thackeray vs Charles Dickens
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Charles Dickens achieved nationwide fame with The Pickwick Papers in 1836–1837, a decade before Thackeray published his satirical Victorian panorama Vanity Fair in 1847–1848.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 5 · Duel #3
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Alfred Tennyson published In Memoriam A.H.H. in 1850 (the year he became Poet Laureate), five years before Robert Browning published his celebrated two-volume collection Men and Women in 1855.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 5 · Duel #4
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: George Eliot's debut full-length novel Adam Bede was published in 1859, twelve years before her masterpiece Middlemarch began publication in parts in 1871–1872.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 5 · Duel #5
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Charles Dickens published the Chancery satire Bleak House in 1852–1853, eight years before Pip's story Great Expectations was serialized in All the Year Round in 1860–1861.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 5 · Duel #6
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
options: Far from the Madding Crowd (Thomas Hardy)
items.explanation: Thomas Hardy published his breakthrough pastoral Wessex novel Far from the Madding Crowd in 1874, seventeen years before the controversial tragedy Tess of the d'Urbervilles in 1891.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 5 · Duel #7
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
options: The Mill on the Floss (George Eliot)
items.explanation: George Eliot published The Mill on the Floss (the tragedy of Maggie and Tom Tulliver) in 1860, sixteen years before her final completed novel Daniel Deronda appeared in 1876.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 5 · Duel #8
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
options: The Picture of Dorian Gray (Oscar Wilde)
items.explanation: Matthew Arnold published his seminal cultural critique Culture and Anarchy in 1869, over two decades before Oscar Wilde published his Aesthetic novel The Picture of Dorian Gray in 1890 (book 1891).

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 5 · Duel #9
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Charles Dickens published his industrial novel Hard Times (set in Coketown) in 1854, seven years before George Eliot published her pastoral fable Silas Marner: The Weaver of Raveloe in 1861.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 5 · Duel #10
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Thomas Hardy published The Mayor of Casterbridge: The Life and Death of a Man of Character in 1886, nine years before his final and most fiercely denounced novel Jude the Obscure in 1895.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 5 · Duel #11
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
options: Goblin Market and Other Poems (Christina Rossetti)
items.explanation: Christina Rossetti published her defining Pre-Raphaelite collection Goblin Market and Other Poems in 1862, six years before William Morris began publishing his epic poem The Earthly Paradise in 1868.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 5 · Duel #12
items.meta: Bram Stoker vs Robert Louis Stevenson
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
options: Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde (Robert Louis Stevenson)
items.explanation: Robert Louis Stevenson published Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde in 1886, eleven years before Bram Stoker published his epistolary vampire classic Dracula in 1897.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 5 · Duel #13
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Elizabeth Gaskell published her condition-of-England novel Mary Barton in 1848, six years before North and South began serialization in Dickens's Household Words in 1854.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 5 · Duel #14
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
options: The Importance of Being Earnest (Oscar Wilde)
items.explanation: Oscar Wilde scored his first major West End theatrical triumph with Lady Windermere's Fan in 1892, three years before his crowning comedic triumph The Importance of Being Earnest premiered in 1895.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 5 · Duel #15
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Thomas Carlyle published his influential socio-economic critique Past and Present in 1843, seventeen years before John Ruskin published his political economy essays Unto This Last in 1860.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 6 · Duel #1
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Joseph Conrad published Heart of Darkness in 1899 (in Blackwood's Magazine; book form 1902), a quarter of a century before E.M. Forster published A Passage to India in 1924.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 6 · Duel #2
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: D.H. Lawrence published his autobiographical mining novel Sons and Lovers in 1913, seven years before Women in Love was privately printed in 1920.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 6 · Duel #3
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
options: The Love Song of J. Alfred Prufrock (T.S. Eliot)
items.explanation: T.S. Eliot published The Love Song of J. Alfred Prufrock in Poetry magazine in 1915 (collection Prufrock and Other Observations 1917), seven years before The Waste Land appeared in 1922.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 6 · Duel #4
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
options: A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man (James Joyce)
items.explanation: James Joyce published A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man in 1916 (after serializing in The Egoist), six years before Sylvia Beach published Ulysses in Paris on Joyce's 40th birthday in 1922.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 6 · Duel #5
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Aldous Huxley published his complex musicalized novel of ideas Point Counter Point in 1928, four years before his dystopian classic Brave New World was published in 1932.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 6 · Duel #6
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Virginia Woolf published Mrs Dalloway through the Hogarth Press in May 1925, two years before To the Lighthouse was published in May 1927.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 6 · Duel #7
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
options: The Wild Swans at Coole (W.B. Yeats)
items.explanation: W.B. Yeats published The Wild Swans at Coole in 1917 (expanded 1919), nearly a decade before his monumental late collection The Tower was published in 1928.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 6 · Duel #8
items.meta: George Bernard Shaw vs George Bernard Shaw
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: George Bernard Shaw wrote Pygmalion in 1912 (staged 1913/1914), more than a decade before his historical tragedy Saint Joan premiered in New York in 1923.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 6 · Duel #9
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: D.H. Lawrence published The Rainbow in 1915 (it was prosecuted and banned under the Obscene Publications Act), sixteen years before Woolf published her poetic soliloquy novel The Waves in 1931.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 6 · Duel #10
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
options: Where Angels Fear to Tread (E.M. Forster)
items.explanation: E.M. Forster published his debut novel Where Angels Fear to Tread in 1905, nearly two decades before his final novel A Passage to India was published in 1924.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 6 · Duel #11
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: T.S. Eliot published his major conversion poem Ash-Wednesday in 1930, over a decade before the four parts of Four Quartets were first gathered into a single volume in 1943.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 6 · Duel #12
items.meta: Ford Madox Ford vs Ford Madox Ford
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Ford Madox Ford published his classic unreliable-narrator novel The Good Soldier in 1915, nearly a decade before Some Do Not... (1924), the opening volume of his tetralogy Parade's End.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 6 · Duel #13
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: James Joyce published his Dublin short story collection Dubliners in 1914, a quarter of a century before his revolutionary polyglot work Finnegans Wake appeared in 1939.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 6 · Duel #14
items.meta: George Bernard Shaw vs George Bernard Shaw
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: George Bernard Shaw's Salvation Army satire Major Barbara premiered in 1905, fourteen years before Heartbreak House: A Fantasia in the Russian Manner on English Themes was published in 1919.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 6 · Duel #15
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Virginia Woolf published her playful gender-bending history Orlando: A Biography in 1928, thirteen years before her final pageant novel Between the Acts was published posthumously in 1941.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 7 · Duel #1
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: George Orwell published his anti-Stalinist allegorical novella Animal Farm in August 1945, four years before his dystopian novel Nineteen Eighty-Four appeared in June 1949.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 7 · Duel #2
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
options: The Power and the Glory (Graham Greene)
items.explanation: Graham Greene published his Mexican whisky priest novel The Power and the Glory in 1940, fourteen years before William Golding's debut allegory Lord of the Flies was published in 1954.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 7 · Duel #3
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Samuel Beckett's En attendant Godot premiered on the Parisian stage in 1953 (English version 1955), four years before his claustrophobic one-act masterpiece Endgame premiered in 1957.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 7 · Duel #4
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Harold Pinter's comedy of menace The Birthday Party premiered in 1958 (written 1957), seven years before his full-length drama The Homecoming took the stage in 1965.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 7 · Duel #5
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
options: Rosencrantz and Guildenstern Are Dead (Tom Stoppard)
items.explanation: John Osborne's Jimmy Porter electrified British theater with Look Back in Anger in May 1956, a decade before Tom Stoppard's meta-theatrical triumph at the Edinburgh Fringe in 1966.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 7 · Duel #6
items.meta: Ngũgĩ wa Thiong'o vs Chinua Achebe
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
options: A Grain of Wheat (Ngũgĩ wa Thiong'o)
items.explanation: Chinua Achebe published Things Fall Apart in 1958, nearly a decade before Kenyan novelist Ngũgĩ wa Thiong'o published his Mau Mau rebellion masterpiece A Grain of Wheat in 1967.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 7 · Duel #7
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Doris Lessing published Anna Wulf's fragmented story in The Golden Notebook in 1962, seven years before John Fowles published his metafictional Victorian romance The French Lieutenant's Woman in 1969.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 7 · Duel #8
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Iris Murdoch published her philosophical picaresque debut Under the Net in 1954, twelve years before Jean Rhys published her Jane Eyre prequel Wide Sargasso Sea in 1966.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 7 · Duel #9
items.meta: Wole Soyinka vs Ngũgĩ wa Thiong'o
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
options: Death and the King's Horseman (Wole Soyinka)
items.explanation: Wole Soyinka published his Yoruba tragedy Death and the King's Horseman in 1975, two years before Ngũgĩ wa Thiong'o published his politically subversive novel Petals of Blood in 1977.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 7 · Duel #10
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: J.M. Coetzee published Waiting for the Barbarians in 1980, nineteen years before his second Booker Prize-winning novel Disgrace was published in 1999.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 7 · Duel #11
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
options: A House for Mr Biswas (V.S. Naipaul)
items.explanation: V.S. Naipaul published his semi-autobiographical comic epic A House for Mr Biswas in 1961, a decade before his Booker Prize-winning In a Free State appeared in 1971.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 7 · Duel #12
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Derek Walcott's Obie-winning Caribbean play Dream on Monkey Mountain was first performed in 1967 and published in 1970, two decades before his epic poem Omeros in 1990.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 7 · Duel #13
items.meta: Gabriel García Márquez vs Gabriel García Márquez
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
options: One Hundred Years of Solitude (Gabriel García Márquez)
The Autumn of the Patriarch (Gabriel García Márquez)
items.explanation: Gabriel García Márquez published Cien años de soledad (One Hundred Years of Solitude) in 1967, eight years before his dictator novel El otoño del patriarca (The Autumn of the Patriarch) in 1975.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 7 · Duel #14
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
options: The Remains of the Day (Kazuo Ishiguro)
A Pale View of Hills (Kazuo Ishiguro)
items.explanation: Kazuo Ishiguro made his literary debut with A Pale View of Hills in 1982, seven years before his Booker Prize-winning novel of English restraint The Remains of the Day was published in 1989.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 7 · Duel #15
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Caryl Churchill's feminist drama Top Girls premiered at the Royal Court Theatre in 1982, eleven years before Tom Stoppard's drama of mathematics, landscape, and time Arcadia premiered in 1993.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 8 · Duel #1
items.meta: Salman Rushdie vs Mulk Raj Anand
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Mulk Raj Anand published his groundbreaking social-realist debut Untouchable in 1935 (with an introduction by E.M. Forster), forty-six years before Salman Rushdie's Midnight's Children in 1981.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 8 · Duel #2
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: R.K. Narayan introduced the fictional town of Malgudi in Swami and Friends in 1935, twenty-three years before publishing his Sahitya Akademi Award-winning novel The Guide in 1958.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 8 · Duel #3
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
options: A Sheaf Gleaned in French Fields (Toru Dutt)
items.explanation: Toru Dutt published her poetry collection A Sheaf Gleaned in French Fields in 1876, over six decades before Raja Rao published his landmark Gandhian novel Kanthapura in 1938.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 8 · Duel #4
items.meta: Mulk Raj Anand vs Raja Rao
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
options: The Serpent and the Rope (Raja Rao)
items.explanation: Mulk Raj Anand published his tragic picaresque novel Coolie in 1936, twenty-four years before Raja Rao published his philosophical masterpiece The Serpent and the Rope in 1960.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 8 · Duel #5
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Anita Desai published her Booker-shortlisted Old Delhi family saga Clear Light of Day in 1980, eight years before Amitav Ghosh published his Sahitya Akademi-winning novel The Shadow Lines in 1988.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 8 · Duel #6
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: R.K. Narayan published the final volume of his autobiographical trilogy The English Teacher in 1945, sixteen years before The Man-Eater of Malgudi (introducing Vasu) appeared in 1961.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 8 · Duel #7
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
options: The God of Small Things (Arundhati Roy)
items.explanation: Rohinton Mistry published his debut novel Such a Long Journey in 1991, six years before Arundhati Roy won the Booker Prize with The God of Small Things in 1997.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 8 · Duel #8
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Nissim Ezekiel launched modern Indian English poetry with his debut collection A Time to Change in 1952 (Fortune Press, London), thirteen years before publishing The Exact Name in 1965.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 8 · Duel #9
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Kamala Das published her sensational confessional debut collection Summer in Calcutta in 1965, one year before A.K. Ramanujan published his celebrated first poetry collection The Striders in 1966.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 8 · Duel #10
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Anita Desai made her literary debut with the psychological novel Cry, the Peacock in 1963, fourteen years before her Sahitya Akademi-winning novel Fire on the Mountain in 1977.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 8 · Duel #11
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Amitav Ghosh made his novelistic debut with The Circle of Reason in 1986, fourteen years before his sweeping colonial epic The Glass Palace was published in 2000.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 8 · Duel #12
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Salman Rushdie published his fifth major novel The Moor's Last Sigh in 1995, thirteen years before Aravind Adiga won the Booker Prize with The White Tiger in 2008.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 8 · Duel #13
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Vikram Seth published his novel-in-verse The Golden Gate (written in Onegin stanzas) in 1986, seven years before his epic prose novel A Suitable Boy appeared in 1993.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 8 · Duel #14
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Khushwant Singh published his iconic Partition novel Train to Pakistan (originally titled Mano Majra) in 1956, nearly three decades before Anita Desai published In Custody in 1984.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 8 · Duel #15
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
options: English, August: An Indian Story (Upamanyu Chatterjee)
items.explanation: Upamanyu Chatterjee published his bureaucratic coming-of-age cult classic English, August in 1988, eighteen years before Kiran Desai won the Booker Prize for The Inheritance of Loss in 2006.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 9 · Duel #1
items.meta: Sir Philip Sidney vs John Dryden
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
options: An Apology for Poetry (Sir Philip Sidney)
An Essay of Dramatic Poesy (John Dryden)
items.explanation: Sir Philip Sidney wrote An Apology for Poetry (Defence of Poesie) around 1579–1580 (published 1595), more than seven decades before John Dryden published An Essay of Dramatic Poesy in 1668.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 9 · Duel #2
items.meta: Samuel Taylor Coleridge vs William Wordsworth
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: William Wordsworth published his revolutionary poetic manifesto Preface to Lyrical Ballads in 1800 (expanded 1802), seventeen years before Coleridge critiqued it in Biographia Literaria (1817).

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 9 · Duel #3
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
options: Tradition and the Individual Talent (T.S. Eliot)
items.explanation: Matthew Arnold introduced the 'touchstone method' and 'high seriousness' in The Study of Poetry in 1880, nearly four decades before T.S. Eliot published Tradition and the Individual Talent in 1919.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 9 · Duel #4
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: I.A. Richards published Principles of Literary Criticism in 1924, six years before his brilliant student William Empson published Seven Types of Ambiguity in 1930.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 9 · Duel #5
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Cleanth Brooks published his classic New Critical study of poetry The Well Wrought Urn in 1947, a full decade before Northrop Frye published his archetypal framework Anatomy of Criticism in 1957.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 9 · Duel #6
items.meta: Jacques Derrida vs Ferdinand de Saussure
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
options: Course in General Linguistics (Ferdinand de Saussure)
items.explanation: Ferdinand de Saussure's foundational structuralist lectures Course in General Linguistics were published posthumously in 1916, over half a century before Jacques Derrida inaugurated deconstruction in Of Grammatology (1967).

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 9 · Duel #7
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
options: The Death of the Author (Roland Barthes)
items.explanation: Roland Barthes published his famous essay 'The Death of the Author' in 1967 (in the American journal Aspen), to which Michel Foucault responded in 1969 with his lecture 'What Is an Author?' (Qu'est-ce qu'un auteur?).

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 9 · Duel #8
items.meta: Sandra Gilbert & Susan Gubar vs Edward Said
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
options: The Madwoman in the Attic (Gilbert & Gubar)
items.explanation: Edward Said published Orientalism in 1978, founding modern postcolonial studies one year before Sandra Gilbert and Susan Gubar published their landmark feminist study The Madwoman in the Attic in 1979.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 9 · Duel #9
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Judith Fetterley published The Resisting Reader: A Feminist Approach to American Fiction in 1978, twelve years before Judith Butler formulated gender performativity in Gender Trouble in 1990.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 9 · Duel #10
items.meta: Homi Bhabha vs Gayatri Chakravorty Spivak
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Gayatri Chakravorty Spivak published her seminal deconstructive subaltern essay 'Can the Subaltern Speak?' in 1988, six years before Homi Bhabha gathered his essays on mimicry and hybridity in The Location of Culture (1994).

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 9 · Duel #11
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
options: Postmodernism, or, The Cultural Logic of Late Capitalism (Fredric Jameson)
items.explanation: Terry Eagleton published his bestselling primer Literary Theory: An Introduction in 1983, eight years before Fredric Jameson published his expanded landmark book Postmodernism, or, The Cultural Logic of Late Capitalism in 1991.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 9 · Duel #12
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
options: The Wretched of the Earth (Frantz Fanon)
items.explanation: Frantz Fanon published his psychoanalytic study of anti-Black racism Black Skin, White Masks (Peau noire, masques blancs) in 1952, nine years before his anti-colonial manifesto The Wretched of the Earth (Les Damnés de la Terre) in 1961.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 9 · Duel #13
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Roland Barthes published S/Z (his structuralist/poststructuralist reading of Balzac's Sarrasine) in 1970, five years before Michel Foucault published his analysis of the prison and surveillance Discipline and Punish in 1975.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 9 · Duel #14
items.meta: Edward Said vs Ashcroft, Griffiths & Tiffin
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
options: The Empire Writes Back (Ashcroft, Griffiths & Tiffin)
items.explanation: Bill Ashcroft, Gareth Griffiths, and Helen Tiffin published The Empire Writes Back in 1989, four years before Edward Said published Culture and Imperialism in 1993.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 9 · Duel #15
items.meta: W.K. Wimsatt & Monroe Beardsley vs Claude Lévi-Strauss
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
options: The Structural Study of Myth (Claude Lévi-Strauss)
items.explanation: W.K. Wimsatt and Monroe Beardsley published their foundational New Critical article 'The Intentional Fallacy' in The Sewanee Review in 1946, nine years before Claude Lévi-Strauss published 'The Structural Study of Myth' in 1955.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 10 · Duel #1
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: T.S. Eliot's The Waste Land was published in 1922 (in The Criterion and The Dial), three years before Virginia Woolf published Mrs Dalloway in 1925.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 10 · Duel #2
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: In the miraculous modernist year of 1922, Sylvia Beach published James Joyce's Ulysses in Paris on February 2, 1922, months BEFORE T.S. Eliot's The Waste Land appeared in October 1922.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 10 · Duel #3
items.meta: Virginia Woolf vs F. Scott Fitzgerald
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: F. Scott Fitzgerald published The Great Gatsby in April 1925, two years before Virginia Woolf published To the Lighthouse in May 1927.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 10 · Duel #4
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: T.S. Eliot published The Hollow Men ('This is the way the world ends / Not with a bang but a whimper') in 1925, five years before his conversion poem Ash-Wednesday was published in 1930.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 10 · Duel #5
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
options: The Sound and the Fury (William Faulkner)
items.explanation: Ernest Hemingway published his Lost Generation novel The Sun Also Rises in 1926, three years before William Faulkner published his southern Gothic masterpiece The Sound and the Fury in 1929.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 10 · Duel #6
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
options: A Tale of Two Cities (Charles Dickens)
items.explanation: Charles Dickens published Hard Times in 1854, five years before his historical novel of the French Revolution A Tale of Two Cities was serialized in 1859.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 10 · Duel #7
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: George Eliot published her political novel Felix Holt, the Radical in 1866, five years before Middlemarch began its publication run in 1871–1872.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 10 · Duel #8
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Thomas Hardy published The Mayor of Casterbridge in May 1886, one year before he published The Woodlanders in March 1887.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 10 · Duel #9
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
options: The Return of the Native (Thomas Hardy)
items.explanation: Thomas Hardy published The Return of the Native (introducing Eustacia Vye and Egdon Heath) in 1878, thirteen years before Tess of the d'Urbervilles was published in 1891.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 10 · Duel #10
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: D.H. Lawrence published Sons and Lovers in 1913, two years before The Rainbow was published and subsequently banned in 1915.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 10 · Duel #11
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: The Rainbow (1915) is the first half of Lawrence's Brangwen family saga; its sequel Women in Love was completed shortly after but delayed by censorship until 1920.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 10 · Duel #12
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Joseph Conrad published his London espionage novel The Secret Agent in 1907, four years before his Russian political novel Under Western Eyes appeared in 1911.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 10 · Duel #13
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Samuel Beckett published his French trilogy novel Molloy in 1951, two years before Waiting for Godot had its theatrical premiere at the Théâtre de Babylone in 1953.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 10 · Duel #14
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Salman Rushdie published Midnight's Children in 1981, two years before he published Shame (his satire on Pakistani political dynastic rivalries) in 1983.

items.title: Game 2 (⚡ Which Came First?) · Level 10 · Duel #15
items.stem: Which of these two works was published / composed FIRST?
items.explanation: Salman Rushdie published Shame in 1983, five years before the controversial publication of The Satanic Verses in September 1988.
